title: How long is the height B Y to the longer side?
description: A triangle has a base of six units, a height of four units to it, and another side of eight units. The area is found once, then written a second way with the long side as the base, and the two equal areas give the second height as three units.
teaching_notes: One idea: one triangle has one area, so half of one base times its height equals half of another base times its height. Watch for students who think every height of a triangle has the same length.

video_script.why: The child applies the two bases, one area method of the solved example to find the height BY in a new triangle.
video_script.substitution: Write the area with the base BC and height AX, then again with the base AC and height BY, and make the two equal.
video_script.anchor: the book's triangle ABC with the height AX = 4 to BC = 6, the side AC = 8 and the dotted height BY to AC
never_show: the answer before the answer beat
maths_rules: AC = 8 is longer than BC = 6, so its height BY = 3 is shorter than AX = 4
video_script.design: One triangle all video. One area is written two ways, and the equal areas give the second height.

narration: <bookmark mark='rule'/>Step one, find the area using the base B C and the height eigh X.
<bookmark mark='calc'/>Half of six times four is twelve square units.

narration: <bookmark mark='same'/>Step three, it is the same triangle, so the two areas must be equal.
<bookmark mark='eq'/>Four times B Y is twelve.

narration: <bookmark mark='div'/>Step four, divide twelve by four to get three.
<bookmark mark='chk'/>Check it. Half of eight times three is twelve, the same area.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>B Y is three units.
